This is outstanding! Getting 4 cheap radios to operate coherently (in phase, etc) requires extra hardware but not much. In the old days we used a 4 channel phase comparator on the antenna array with one radio but this has vastly more utility in mapping RF.
YouTube

Watch on YouTube

1164826996901175297.a: This is what we used in the 90s or so. 4 antennas plugged into this unit and the radio would plug into the back. These are meant for 150 MHz marine radios but they work 118-174 or 400-480 MHz depending on model. You only need a single receiver but most of these would pass 25W RF. t.co

1164827662658834432.a: What makes this RTL-SDR based system so much better is that we often spent 1 hour finding which 3 or 4 block area the transmitter was located in but reflections and such had us spend another hour driving in circles looking in the dark with binoculars.

1164831146892414977.a: It would be remarkable to sync 4 KerberosSDR physically distant to each other. (e.g. at the corners of a county.) You could turn the map inside out and instantly know the location of any transmitter inside and just outside the covered area. Dump baseband RF for later decoding.

1164832237612781568.a:
With baseband RF you can fingerprint the transmitters and follow individual signals (phones, radios, etc). Imperfections in components make it hard to generate perfect signals. Though SDR transmitters make it easier to mask/ impersonate if you are trying:
